description: Use this when someone asks for the best time to post on TikTok for their account, or when a specific public TikTok account should post. Input: the TikTok username, and optionally the creator’s time zone. It reads the account’s recent public videos and returns, for each 3-hour window and each weekday in which the account posted, how many videos were posted and their median views against the account’s typical views, plus the window with the highest median when at least two windows hold 2 or more videos. When the niche is clear from the captions, it adds when other creators’ stored posts in that niche were posted, as a secondary signal. It only compares past posting times with public view counts: it cannot see when followers are online, and a few videos are a weak signal. It does not predict or promise views.

time_zone.description: Optional. The creator’s time zone as an IANA name, for example America/New_York. Leave out to use UTC. Text.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.

name: get_tiktok_posting_times

highest_median_window.description: The window with the highest median views among windows holding 2 or more videos. null when fewer than two windows hold 2 or more videos. Something to test, not a finding about followers.

message.description: One or two plain sentences that say what was found or what went wrong.

most_posted_window.description: The 3-hour clock window (the same windows as time_windows) in which the account posts most often. `of` counts every dated recent video, the ones under 3 days old too.

niche_post_times.description: Only when the niche is clear from the captions and stored posts exist: when OTHER creators’ stored posts in that niche were posted. A secondary signal.

status.description: ok, or the plain reason there is no result (not_found, private, no_videos, videos_unavailable, not_enough_videos, invalid_input, unknown_niche, niche_needed, no_data, rate_limited, paused, off, busy, unavailable).

time_windows.description: Each 3-hour clock window in which this account posted: how many of the counted videos, their median views, and that median against the account’s typical views.

time_zone.description: The clock the windows are on. UTC when no time zone was given.

videos_counted.description: Recent public videos at least 3 days old with a date and a view count.

title: Posting times for a TikTok account
